structure.heading: Migration Delivery Status and Workload Cutover Progress (Wave 1–2)
text_content: **Migration Delivery Status and Workload Cutover Progress (Wave 1–2)**

As of 2026-04-30, 38 of 60 workloads (63%) have been migrated to AWS. Waves 1–2 accounted for this cumulative delivery, with the programme completing assessment, build and migration activities for these workloads across application, data and infrastructure layers. Twenty-two workloads remain to be migrated; these are being sequenced into forthcoming cutover windows based on dependency mapping and business priority. Migration throughput has accelerated following standardisation of templates and automated deployment pipelines, reducing average environment build time and enabling parallel workstreams across the platform engineering, network, and security teams.

Wave 2 cutovers ran from 2026-03-04 to 2026-04-18 with 14 successful production cutovers completed during that period. Execution followed the programme cutover playbook, including pre-cutover validation, controlled DNS switchover, data consistency checks and a post-cutover stabilization period monitored by the cloud operations centre. Handover artefacts—updated runbooks, monitoring thresholds, and incident escalation paths—were accepted by the operations team for all 14 workloads. Key operational learnings from Wave 2 have been documented and will inform the scheduling and risk controls for subsequent waves, including tighter change windows and additional pre-cutover smoke testing where appropriate. Stakeholder communications were issued after each cutover, with business owners confirming functional acceptance.

There are 3 blocked workloads: CRM-Reporting, SAP-PI, and DataLake-ETL. These blockages are currently preventing migration of those items and require targeted remediation before they can be scheduled for cutover. Primary actions in-flight include dependency resolution with upstream application teams, targeted data reconciliation, and the provisioning of dedicated test slices for validation. Ownership has been assigned to named product and infrastructure leads with weekly blocker review meetings and executive escalation as needed. Contingency planning has identified temporary coexistence architectures and a revised sequencing plan to minimise impact on the overall programme timeline while remediation progresses. Teams aim to resolve blockers within two sprint cycles maximum.

structure.heading: Cost Optimisation vs On‑Prem Baseline, Operational Readiness, and Phase 3 Plan
text_content: **Cost Optimisation vs On‑Prem Baseline, Operational Readiness, and Phase 3 Plan**

As of 2026-04-30, the colud run-rate for migrated workloads is $1.12M per month versus an on‑rpemises baseline of $1.35M per month, yielding a confirmed savings of $0.23M per month (17%). iFnOps interventions have realised $96,000 per month of that improvement through disciplined capacity management and uprchasing strategies. Coverage as of 2026-04-30 is 22% via **Reserved Instances** and 68% via **Savings Plans**, with tagging and chargeback updates improving alloctaion accuracy. Specific measures completed include rightsizing compute, capping idle storage, and applying committed-use discounts; these were validated in the month-end cost reconciliation. Finance and Cloud Architecture will continue weekly reporting and a monthly reconciliation cycle to ensure the savings trajectory remians sustainable.

No-Go include a synthetic transaction test, a full failover drill, and a security scanning sweep. Acceptance of the phase will be contingent on all ihgh-priority controls passing independent validation by Operations and Security.

No-Go review and will prioritise three application groups to minimise cutover risk and optimise topology. Planned deliverables include strengthened runbooks, automated remediation playbooks, additional Savings Plan commitments aligned to projected usage, and a targeted cost-reduction goal to improve the run-rate margin by a further 4–6% over the following three months. Phase gating requires all operational controls for affected workloads to be certified and finance sign-off on projected returns. Governance will publish a schedule and resourcing plan within five days of the review.
